Context/Background: In a prospective endometrial carcinoma (EC) cohort, we performed a differential analysis of protein levels between hotspot-mutated CTNNB1 and WT CTNNB1 tumors, in the CNV-L subgroup.  In a separate analysis, we found that CTNNB1 S45 phosphorylation was significantly downregulated in hotspot-mutated tumors, whereas phosphosites distant from the hotspot mutations were mostly upregulated.
Prompt: Provide a discussion of the results from the differential analysis and any relevance to the mutation state of CTNNB1.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
In a prospective endometrial carcinoma cohort (CNV-L subgroup), global proteomic profiling (NIHMS1921121-supplement-7-CTNNB1HotspotvsWT-Protein.csv; total_rows = 10 150) compared hotspot-mutant CTNNB1 tumors to CTNNB1-WT.  Although CTNNB1 S45 phosphorylation was reported to be downregulated in mutants (not specified here), a broad set of other phosphosites and total protein levels were measured.  Key differential protein hits included AXIN1 (L2FC = 0.672, FDR = 1.9 × 10⁻¹²), CTNNB1 (0.760, FDR = 1.7 × 10⁻¹¹), DKK4 (4.05, FDR = 6.4 × 10⁻⁸), LEF1 (1.31, FDR = 6.4 × 10⁻⁸) and LRP4 (1.55, FDR = 8.4 × 10⁻⁷).  For details not given (e.g., sample numbers, replicates), we state “not specified.”

Keywords  
• Wnt signaling  
• CTNNB1 hotspot mutation  
• β-catenin phosphorylation (S45)  
• Proteostasis/ER processing  
• Mitochondrial translation

Candidate Genes  
CTNNB1, AXIN1, DKK4, LEF1, LRP4, DKK1, WIF1

Pathway Enrichments  
Across four gene-set libraries, directionality of enrichment was as follows (counts_by_database):

• KEGG_2016: 31 up, 52 down (37% up, 63% down; ratio = 0.60)  
• GO_Biological_Process_2023: 197 up, 267 down (42% up, 58% down; ratio = 0.74)  
• Reactome_Pathways_2024: 164 up, 114 down (59% up, 41% down; ratio = 1.44)  
• MSigDB_Hallmark_2020: 12 up, 11 down (52% up, 48% down; ratio = 1.09)

| Wnt signaling pathway (hsa04310)                   | Up        | DKK4, PLCB4, WIF1, CTNNB1, DKK1, NOTUM, CTNNBIP1, WNT11, AXIN1, FZD3, RAC3, CCND1, FZD1, MMP7, TCF7, LEF1 |

Analysis  
1. Wnt pathway proteins are uniformly upregulated in CTNNB1-mutant tumors: CTNNB1 itself (L2FC = 0.76), its destruction-complex partner AXIN1 (0.67), transcriptional effectors LEF1 (1.31) and TCF7, and secreted antagonists DKK1/4 and WIF1.  GSEA identified “Wnt-beta catenin signaling” (MSigDB_Hallmark_2020; NES = 3.66, FDR = 1.1 × 10⁻³) and “Wnt signaling pathway” (KEGG_2016; NES = 4.50, FDR = 3.9 × 10⁻⁴).  
2. The downregulation of CTNNB1 S45 phosphorylation in hotspot mutants likely impairs β-catenin degradation, consistent with increased total CTNNB1 and target activation.  
3. Proteostasis and ER-processing pathways (“Protein processing in ER”; NES = 5.74) were also upregulated, suggesting elevated folding demand in CTNNB1-mutant cells.  
4. Mitochondrial gene expression/translation and OxPhos signatures are strongly up, indicating metabolic rewiring.  
5. Complement/coagulation cascades are the main downregulated KEGG_2016 module (NES = –5.15), pointing to immunomodulatory shifts.

Keyword-Guided Subset (Wnt-Focused)  
| Database                   | Pathway                                              | NES    | FDR           | Leading Genes                                              |
|----------------------------|------------------------------------------------------|--------|---------------|------------------------------------------------------------|
| KEGG_2016                  | Wnt signaling pathway (hsa04310)                     | 4.497  | 3.88 × 10⁻⁴ | DKK4, PLCB4, WIF1, CTNNB1, DKK1, NOTUM, CTNNBIP1, WNT11, AXIN1, FZD3, RAC3, CCND1, FZD1, MMP7, TCF7, LEF1 |
| GO_Biological_Process_2023 | Regulation Of Wnt Signaling Pathway (GO:0030111)     | 3.531  | 2.91 × 10⁻² | DKK4, WIF1, APCDD1, DKK1, NOTUM, CTNND2, CTNNBIP1, APP      |
| Reactome_Pathways_2024     | TCF Dependent Signaling in Response to WNT           | 3.453  | 2.01 × 10⁻² | DKK4, WIF1, CTNNB1, DKK1, AXIN1, TCF7, LEF1                |
| MSigDB_Hallmark_2020       | Wnt-beta Catenin Signaling                           | 3.660  | 1.15 × 10⁻³ | DKK4, PSEN2, CTNNB1, DKK1, AXIN1, TCF7, LEF1               |

Key Genes/Proteins (Leading Edge)  
Upregulated  
| Gene    | Direction | Role/Function                                     | Pathway(s)                  |
|---------|-----------|---------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------|
| CTNNB1  | Up        | Core effector of Wnt/β-catenin transcription      | Wnt signaling, EMT, Myc     |
| DKK4    | Up        | Secreted Wnt antagonist; feedback regulator       | Wnt signaling               |
| LEF1    | Up        | β-catenin–dependent transcription factor          | Wnt signaling               |

Downregulated  
| Gene    | Direction | Role/Function                                     | Pathway(s)                  |
|---------|-----------|---------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------|
| SFRP4   | Down      | Secreted Frizzled-related Wnt modulator           | Wnt signaling               |
| ANXA8L1 | Down      | Annexin family; membrane organization             | Vesicle trafficking         |
| FOXA1   | Down      | Pioneer transcription factor in endometrial cells | Hormone signaling           |

Comparisons & Confidence  
• The proteomic shifts in Wnt pathway components mirror the hotspot mutation’s effect on S45 dephosphorylation, supporting a model of β-catenin stabilization.  
• Concordant upregulation of ER folding and mitochondrial translation pathways suggests coordinated increases in protein synthesis and energy production.  
• Downregulation of ECM and immune-related modules (complement cascade) may reflect tumor microenvironment remodeling.  
• Single-modality findings (e.g., complement downregulation) should be confirmed by orthogonal assays (transcriptomics/immunohistochemistry).

Implications  
• CTNNB1 hotspot mutations drive persistent Wnt pathway activation via both reduced degradation (S45) and increased transcriptional machinery (LEF1/TCF7).  
• Feedback antagonists (DKK1/4, WIF1) are induced but insufficient to counteract pathway hyperactivation—targeting these or downstream effectors (e.g., TCF/LEF inhibitors) may restore control.  
• Elevated proteostasis and mitochondrial programs reveal metabolic vulnerabilities; agents that impair ER stress responses or mitochondrial translation may synergize with Wnt pathway blockade.

Next Steps & Clarification  
1. Validate S45 dephosphorylation effect on β-catenin half-life and nuclear localization in CTNNB1-mutant EC cells.  
2. Perform phospho-proteomic profiling of other CTNNB1 sites to map compensatory phosphorylation.  
3. Test Wnt pathway inhibitors (PORCN inhibitors, tankyrase inhibitors) in mutant versus WT EC cell models.  
4. Examine complement pathway protein levels in the microenvironment by IHC to confirm proteomics.
